28/02/2020

Dr Maureen Martinson

General pPractitioner

Tambo Medical Centre

Commented [OETONLIN1]: Capitalise all words when
addressing someone by their professional title.

18 Tamborine Drive

Mt Tamborine QLD

Dear Dr Martinson,

Re: Mr Kenneth Phillips, DOB: 05/05/1974

Thank you for accepting Mr Phillips into your care, who requires your ongoing support following a
bilateral lung transplant due to a history of interstitial lung disease.

On 10/01/2020, Mr Phillips was admitted for his surgery after which he was transferred to our
Rehabilitation Ward five days later. After his operation, he used nebulizer 2L, his oxygen saturation was
99% and refused to stop oxygen. He had a stage two painful pressure ulcer in the coccyx for which it
requires 2 Nd daily dressing, a pressure relief mattress, cushion and regular Panadol. He was able to
walk with a four-wheel walker for 20 meters with shortness of breath after which he used a single point
stick without shortness of breath.

Two weeks later, Mr Phillips agreed to reduce the nebulizer to 1L and to be discharged to home without
oxygen since his oxygen saturation was 97%. He was educated about home oxygen and started self-
medicating with supervision. Today, his room air oxygen saturation was 94%, he can mobilize without
aids and self-medicate well under supervision. The coccyx wound needs dressing every second day after
his discharge as he will be discharged on 01/03/2020.

He is divorced, works as a builder and lives alone as his son lives away from home. He will be moving to
Mt Tamborine to live with his sister, who is a nurse, and has offered to help with his wound dressing and
medication. Kindly note, a list of medications is enclosed.
